case_name: U.P. State Road Transport Corporation v Man Singh
respondent:
Man Singh
Supreme Court of India

13 September 2006
Appeal (Civil) 4107 of 2006
The Judgment was delivered by : S. B. Sinha, J.
1. Delay condoned.
2. Leave granted.
3.  The appellant before us is a Corporation constituted under the Road Transport Corporation Act. The respondent was appointed w.e.f. 20.4.1974 on temporary basis. His services were terminated on 23.07.1975. He is said to have been paid one month's salary in lieu of notice. Some allegations had also been made that he committed misconduct.

facts: The respondent was appointed by the appellant Corporation on a temporary basis in 1974, but his services were terminated in 1975.
Some allegations had also been made that he committed misconduct.
He raised an industrial dispute in 1986 which was referred to for adjudication to the Presiding Officer, Labour Court, U.P., Agra.

The industrial dispute referred by the appropriate Government for its adjudication by the Labour Court reads as under: 'That the act of the employer in terminating the service of their workman Man Singh s/o Sher Singh, post Conductor, vide order dated 23.03.1975 is proper and/or legal. If not then to what relief/compensation is the concerned workman entitled for and with what further details.'
The Labour Court set aside the order of termination of the services of the respondent but granted back-wages only from 1986.
The High Court in the writ petition filed by the appellant refused to interfere therewith.
issues: Whether the Labour Court had jurisdiction to pass an award directing reinstatement of the respondent
Whether the respondent was entitled to reinstatement or compensation
court_reasoning: While exercising the power under Section 11A of the Industrial Disputes Act, the Labour Court should have taken into consideration all relevant factors.
The respondent does not dispute that he got employment only for about a year during the period 24.4.1974 to 23.7.1975.
There is nothing on record to show that he was employed in accordance with the recruitment rules framed by the Appellant Corporation.

No material has also been brought on record to show that the vacancy was a regular one or in filling up of the said vacancy the constitutional requirements as envisaged under Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India were complied with.
holding: The appeal is allowed to the extent mentioned hereinbefore.

The appellant is directed to pay a sum of Rs.50,000/- to the respondent within a period of eight weeks from today, failing which, the same shall carry interest at the rate of 6 per cent per annum till the date of actual payment.
